thread:
elaine (support): heads up — AcmeCo reporting intermittent 502/504s hitting our hosted inference endpoint (api.redwood.ai/v1/generate). They see TLS handshake timeouts mainly from eu-west-1 and us-east-1. First report at 2026-03-13T10:02:03Z. Customer says errors started ~10:00Z and are still reproducible from their side.

customer-rep (AcmeCo): yes, we started getting these a few minutes ago. curl to the endpoint sometimes returns 502 with SSL errors. other requests succeed. looks like a TLS/connectivity problem.

elaine (support): can you paste the curl output and any client error? any proxy in front?

customer-rep (AcmeCo): here's one sample from our side:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
*   Trying 18.201.12.34:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (18.201.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* SSL connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 
* ALPN, server accepted to use h2
* SSL_read:errno=104
* Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection was reset, errno 104
```

elaine (support): thanks. repeating question — are they behind a corporate proxy? any MTLS?

customer-rep (AcmeCo): standard outbound, no mTLS. We do have internal DNS resolvers that cache aggressively.

matt (oncall): pinging infra — seeing a small spike in 502/504s from our gateway metrics starting 2026-03-13T09:58Z, peaked ~09:59:30Z. Gateway logs show a bunch of TLS handshake timeouts and upstream ECONNRESET. Also noticed a cert-rotation job finished recently (2026-03-13T09:56Z) for api.redwood.ai.

sasha (netops): can you dump the gateway logs for TLS handshake errors to paste here? Also need dig from multiple resolvers to check A records.

chris (prodeng): I pulled the gateway pod logs — snippets: 

```
2026-03-13T09:58:42Z gateway-01 tls_handshake_timeout client=198.51.100.34 reason="handshake timed out after 6s"
2026-03-13T09:58:43Z gateway-02 upstream_reset client=203.0.113.21 backend=10.120.5.12:443 error="EOF"
2026-03-13T09:58:44Z gateway-01 cert_verify_error subject="CN=api.redwood.ai" error="x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
```

chris (prodeng): also see a brief spike of 5xxs in the edge autoscaler logs correlated with a flapping backend pool.

sasha (netops): I ran dig from 3 public resolvers after the report:

```
# dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
18.201.12.34
# dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
18.201.12.34
# dig +short api.redwood.ai @9.9.9.9
(no answer)
```

sasha (netops): interesting — 9.9.9.9 returned no answer at that moment. TTLs are 30s. Could be a transient authoritative resolver issue or DDoS mitigation in front of some resolvers.

matt (oncall): correlating with the cert rotation — deploy-bot shows rotation job finished 2026-03-13T09:56:10Z, then a reloader touched gateway certs and restarted TLS workers at 09:56:25Z. Could be a partial rollout where some workers got the new chain and some cached the old one, causing verification mismatches.

elaine (support): customer says sometimes requests succeed and sometimes fail — that matches a partial pool mismatch or DNS returning different IPs. asking them to run a few quick repros and attach traceroute and dig outputs.

customer-rep (AcmeCo): attached — traceroute to 18.201.12.34 shows one hop timing out then reaches gateway, sometimes different IP returned by dig.

```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (18.201.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.3 ms
 2  203.0.113.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  18.201.12.34  12.4 ms  12.2 ms  12.3 ms
```

matt (oncall): OK. immediate triage plan: 1) pin gateway to previous cert bundle on a canary node to see if failures reduce, 2) check our authoritative DNS for any propagation or NXDOMAIN anomalies, 3) coordinate with CDN/edge provider on resolver anomalies.

sasha (netops): I'm running tcpdump on gateway nodes to capture ClientHello SNI and source IPs. capturing eBPF socket events too to see which backend IPs selected. Will paste pcap excerpt.

sasha (netops): pcap shows some clients sending SNI="api.redwood.ai" and gateway replying with TLSv1.3 ServerHello then immediately reset for a subset of clients (RST). looks like upstream backend refused to serve the connection occasionally.

chris (prodeng): analyzing backend pool — a subset of backends were running old cert bundle (missing intermediate CA) due to a race in the rotation script. That would explain x509 verify errors in the gateway logs. I'm rolling a hotfix to ensure atomic swap of the cert directory and full reload across all workers.

elaine (support): customer — we believe root cause is partial cert rotation + transient resolver failures giving mixed IPs. This can cause some gateways to see old certs and fail verify, while others succeed. We're applying a hotfix now and will monitor.

customer-rep (AcmeCo): thanks, please keep us updated. they are seeing requests succeed now more often but occasional failures remain.

matt (oncall): hotfix deployed 2026-03-13T10:06:12Z — rotation script now uses atomic rename + health check before advertising new certs. Also added a guard to prevent partial rollout. Rolling back is possible but hotfix should converge quickly.

sasha (netops): also confirmed with dig across providers after fix:
```
# before: some resolvers returned no answer
# after:
# dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
18.201.12.34
# dig +short api.redwood.ai @9.9.9.9
18.201.12.34
```

matt (oncall): metrics look back to baseline for 502/504s by 10:10Z. I'll keep the incident open for 2 hours to monitor.

elaine (support): closing loop with customer — sent them repro steps and confirmation of fix; asked them to reopen if they see anything else.

customer-rep (AcmeCo): confirmed — errors dropped significantly. thanks for the quick response.

chris (prodeng): follow-ups for postmortem: add unit test for rotation script, add canary gating to rotation pipeline, add resolver health checks to our infra monitoring, and log SNI mismatch rates.

elaine (support): tagging as support-escalation — will create postmortem doc once Matt/Chris add technical root cause and timeline.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation/job/238 completed status=success duration=00:00:23

matt (oncall): incident -> SEV2 (brief outage risk) created and assigned to prodeng/netops. timeline and notes will be added to incidents channel postmortem.

elaine (support): thanks everyone.
